title: exRNA BioFluids data research method
bodyHtml:
The exRNA Browser

Using 6,532 extracellular RNA (exRNA) profiles from human serum, plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, urine, and saliva across 60 datasets in the exRNA Atlas, this study identifies >17 million genomic loci covering >18% of the human genome expressing exRNA. Analyses demonstrate the potential of this first-of-its-kind exRNA map to provide valuable insights into exRNA biology. They reveal both cross-biofluid and biofluid-specific loci, variability in exRNA abundance across biofluids, and distinct patterns of overlap with the transcribed (GENCODE) and regulatory (ENCODE) loci. The exRNA loci account for a remarkable amount of positive evolutionary selection in primates and mammals and associate with GWAS loci. Notably, previously unconsidered low-abundance exRNA loci show potential as biomarkers for neurodegenerative diseases. To support future exRNA research we develop a comprehensive resource that assigns unique identifiers (exGLid) to each exRNA locus. The loci are annotated with source datasets and analysis results, accessible via user interfaces, APIs, and visualization tools. For more extensive methods, see here.

Start by searching for a gene name or GRCh37/hg19 human genome coordinates.

Filter for results relevant to a specific biofluid(s), exGLid, exRNA Atlas Dataset, gene type, and/or ENCODE regulatory element.
